shots.why: recognizable: a harbor from a plane, 1914. Grain and dust are already moving but it is still a place.
same reel. The white shoreline stays and everything else becomes mottling. Held long enough that the sea starts to read as emulsion: the apparent landscape is the carrier.

following that bright edge to a different film, 1966, where a black arc crosses a tidal flat. Its narrator's Suddenly the whole harbor of Valdez is sucked dry is kept: he is describing an event, the picture is also describing its own surface.
same film, a horse and machine pulled out of white. Whatever damaged it, nobody here is shown as having chosen it.
a recognizable scene comes back through a decayed surface: skaters in a park. The pulse on the track belongs to this source.
end on a blank interval, 1915, with its own recorded noise raised: flecks and hairs and no picture.
